tagline: AWS's open-source orchestrator for multiple AI coding CLIs

scenes.narration: Day 53: CLI Agent Orchestrator, AWS's framework for coordinating multiple AI coding CLIs, tried with Claude Code as the worker.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Runs a local server that tracks terminals and sessions
Starts provider CLIs like Claude Code in tmux panes
A supervisor delegates tasks to workers in parallel
scenes.narration: CAO runs a local server, starts CLI agents such as Claude Code inside tmux panes, and lets a supervisor hand work off to those workers.

steps.narration: A launch command tells the local server to create a session and a worker terminal.
The server opens a tmux pane and types the claude command into it, with the flag that is meant to skip permission prompts.
This was Claude Code's first interactive run in the container, so it showed a theme picker, a security notice, and a folder-trust prompt instead of going idle.
None of those screens cleared automatically, so the wait for an idle worker ran out.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Installing CAO and starting its server worked perfectly. Handing a task to a Claude Code worker did not.
lines: TimeoutError: Claude Code init timed out
scenes.narration: Every install and server-start step worked exactly as documented. Only the supervisor-to-worker handoff failed, with this exact timeout from the server log.
Full write-up, including why we stopped instead of forcing the trust prompt through, is on Zenn.
